name: נְעַרְיָה
gloss: servant (attendant) of Yahweh; or young man of Yahweh
summary: Two men: Neariah son of Shemaiah, of David's line after the exile, father of Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam (1Ch 3:22–23); and Neariah son of Ishi, one of the Simeonite captains who led five hundred men to Mount Seir in the days of Hezekiah and struck the rest of Amalek (1Ch 4:42–43). The name is נַעַר with יָה: the attendant of Yahweh, as the boy Samuel “ministered to Yahweh” (1Sa 2:11; 3:1) and Joshua the נַעַר attended Moses at the tent (Exo 33:11). Scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, וּנְעַרְיָה and Shaphat, six.”
“The sons of נְעַרְיָה: Elioenai, Hizkiah and Azrikam, three.”
“Pelatiah, וּנְעַרְיָה, Rephaiah and Uzziel, the sons of Ishi, at their head.”
“They struck the remnant of the Amalekites who had escaped.”
“The boy (וְהַנַּעַר) Samuel ministered to Yahweh before Eli”: the נַעַר as attendant in Yahweh's service.
“Gehazi, the נַעַר of Elisha”: the word for a master's attendant, with the master's name after it.

note: TIPNR records the two men under their own keys; they bear the same name and are tagged here. The reading takes נַעַר in its sense “attendant” (with a divine name as the master, as Phoenician nʿr is a temple servitor, KAI 37 A 12); “young man of Yahweh” is the other reading of the form. No verse gives the meaning.
